clue.text: Fashions go through various phases

definitions.note: verb: to fashion is to mould or form

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the following word take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Trends in clothing cycle through one stage after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to mould or form it, a verb sense of giving form.

clue.text: Verbal approval of a brace of cooked hare !

indicators.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds, so the piece is taken twice
cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner praising a pair of hares well prepared in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns HARE into HEAR, and 'a brace of' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary shout of agreement is spoken applause for a speaker's point.

clue.text: He couldn't complain of growing pains

definitions.text: He couldn't complain of growing pains

parts.words: He couldn't complain of growing pains
parts.note: the boy in J. M. Barrie's play never grows up, so he can have no aches from growing

explanation.surface: A man who had no grounds to grumble about the aches of adolescence.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's boy who never ages could feel no aches from getting taller.

clue.text: It's illuminating up to a point

definitions.text: It's illuminating up to a point

parts.words: It's illuminating up to a point
parts.note: a lamp beam lights only one small area, a spot, rather than everything; 'up to a point' also means partly

explanation.surface: Something that is only partly enlightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' usually means 'partly'; here it means lighting one point on a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage lamp casting a narrow beam lights one small area of the stage.

clue.text: A visionary is not dependent on this

definitions.text: A visionary is not dependent on this

parts.words: A visionary is not dependent on this
parts.note: a visionary sees things in the mind's eye, so needs no physical power of seeing

explanation.surface: A dreamer or prophet does not rely on something ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary perceives inwardly, so working eyes are not required for the visions.

clue.text: Their recipients are not single-minded

parts.note: those who receive these intend not to stay unmarried

explanation.surface: People who receive something are not focused on one aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single-minded' usually means focused; here it means minded to stay single.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed person wears this band, given at the promise of marriage, so they no longer plan to stay unwed.

clue.text: In the main, insular

parts.note: 'the main' is the sea, and insular means like an island, ringed by water

explanation.surface: A remark that something is, for the most part, narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but is the old word for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounded by ocean on every side, as an island is.

clue.text: One doesn't need a licence to drive it

definitions.text: One doesn't need a licence to drive it

parts.words: One doesn't need a licence to drive it
parts.note: drive here is a long tee shot on the links, not steering a vehicle

explanation.surface: Something that can be driven without any permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tee shot in the game played on links is called a drive, and no permit is needed for that.

clue.text: But it does not necessarily have a floating population

definitions.text: But it does not necessarily have a floating population

parts.words: But it does not necessarily have a floating population
parts.note: the second half of the answer is a vessel that floats, yet this settlement need not float

explanation.surface: A place whose residents are not necessarily transient.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'floating population' usually means transient residents; here it plays on the vessel at the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town or municipal district, especially in South Africa or North America, a kind of settlement.

clue.text: But it is generally rendered in full

definitions.text: But it is generally rendered in full

parts.words: But it is generally rendered in full
parts.note: a piece written in several voices is performed complete, by a full choir, although its name suggests only portions

explanation.surface: An objection: the thing is usually given in its entirety.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'But' plays against the first word of the answer: something named for parts is performed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition for several voice parts is normally sung by the whole choir together.

clue.text: Venerate all who reform

indicators.note: to reform is to make again in a new shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to honour everyone who mends their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to regard as holy, the same as to sanctify or consecrate.

clue.text: Limping cricketer ?

parts.note: a cricketer who limps might be imagined to have one limb shorter than the other; it is also a fielding position

explanation.surface: A cricket player hobbling about with an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a close fielder on the leg side near the batsman stands at a position with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder at the close leg-side position near the batsman is named after that position, and a limp suggests an uneven limb.

clue.text: Cloud of saintly associations

definitions.meaning: a type of rain-bearing grey cloud
a halo of light around a saint's head in paintings

explanation.surface: A cloud with holy connections.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dark rain cloud and the radiant halo painted around holy figures.

clue.text: All agreed there is no occasion for this

definitions.text: All agreed there is no occasion for this

parts.words: All agreed there is no occasion for this
parts.note: when everyone is in accord there is nothing to dispute

explanation.surface: Everyone concurs that something is unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute arises only from disagreement, so unanimity leaves no cause for one.

clue.text: He certainly didn't take a poor view of himself

definitions.text: He certainly didn't take a poor view of himself

parts.words: He certainly didn't take a poor view of himself
parts.note: the Greek youth fell in love with his own reflection in a pool

explanation.surface: A conceited man held himself in high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth tells of a youth who fell in love with his own reflection in water.

clue.text: Architectural bird

definitions.meaning: Sir Christopher, the architect of St Paul's Cathedral; the adjective stands for the famous architect's name

explanation.surface: A bird with a talent for building design.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of St Paul's architect is also a small brown songbird.

clue.text: They have scant regard for their betters

definitions.text: They have scant regard for their betters

parts.words: They have scant regard for their betters
parts.note: betters are people who place bets, whom these cheats refuse to pay

explanation.surface: Snobs who disdain their social superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betters' looks like social superiors but means people who bet; a bookmaker who absconds without paying them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bookmakers or gamblers who fail to pay what they owe on a wager.

clue.text: Needing a change ? Try part of Switzerland

indicators.note: a change means the letters of the preceding words take on a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to try a holiday in the Alps for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NEEDING A into ENGADINE, the valley of the Inn in eastern Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Engadine is an Alpine valley of the River Inn in the Swiss canton of Graubünden.

clue.text: This way for the launch

parts.note: a ship is launched down an inclined ramp into the water; way also suggests a direction sign

explanation.surface: A signpost pointing guests towards a product launch event.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is the sloping ramp from which a newly built ship is launched.

clue.text: To the last of recorded time " (Macbeth)

definitions.text: To the last of recorded time " (Macbeth)

parts.words: To the last of recorded time " (Macbeth)
parts.note: the quotation from the 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow' speech has a word missing before 'of recorded time'

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Macbeth's famous speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's line is 'To the last syllable of recorded time'; the missing word fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word missing from Macbeth's speech is a unit of pronunciation in a word.

clue.text: Conspiracy to fascinate

explanation.surface: A plot designed to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a secret plotting and to arouse keen curiosity.

clue.text: Fish with something in common with the bee ?

definitions.text: Fish with something in common with the bee ?

parts.words: Fish with something in common with the bee ?
parts.note: a flat sea fish whose tail carries a venomous barb, as a bee carries a barb

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which fish resembles a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat ray has a venomous barbed spine on its tail, just as a bee has a barb.

clue.text: Dismissal for wining with Falstaff ?

definitions.meaning: Falstaff's favourite drink was sack, a fortified wine, so drinking it with him

explanation.surface: Getting fired for drinking with Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff, the fat knight in Shakespeare's Henry IV, loves sack, an old name for sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fired from a job, and also drinking the sherry Falstaff loved.

clue.text: Something a runaway makes himself

parts.note: the idiom 'make oneself ___' means to disappear or keep out of the way

explanation.surface: Considering what a fugitive turns himself into.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to make oneself scarce means to leave quickly and stay out of sight, as a fugitive does.

clue.text: It is, in a word, bad in age

definitions.text: It is, in a word, bad in age

parts.words: It is, in a word, bad in age
parts.note: the three words 'bad in age' joined into one word spell badinage, playful banter

explanation.surface: Something described as being poor in its old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' tells you to close up 'bad in age' into the single word badinage, which means teasing banter.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage and this word both mean good-humoured teasing or banter.

clue.text: Methuselah's favourite drink ?

parts.note: Methuselah lived 969 years, so his drink would be one that prolongs life

explanation.surface: Wondering what the Bible's oldest man liked to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived man, so his preferred drink is the alchemists' potion of eternal life.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemical potion believed to grant endless life, ideal for the Bible's longest-lived man.

clue.text: They include courses for horses

parts.note: courses means meal servings, not racecourses; feed bags hung on a horse's head hold its meal

explanation.surface: Racing venues designed for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: These are canvas feed bags hung over a horse's muzzle to hold its meal.

clue.text: Snug nest arranged for potential killers

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A cosy home prepared for creatures that might turn deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges SNUG and NEST into STEN GUNS, the British sub-machine guns of WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: Sten guns are lightweight British sub-machine guns, weapons capable of taking life.

clue.text: Tantrums in the theatre

definitions.meaning: angry outbursts or noisy displays of temper
divisions of a play's acts, or stage settings

explanation.surface: Fits of temper at the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both displays of temper and the divisions or settings of a stage play.
